judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The image has alt="Passados-imaginados.jpg" and the caption 'PASSADOS IMAGINADOS'. It is one of the eleven photos in the 'Conheça nossas novas exposições' auto-scrolling media wheel (premium-adv-carousel, not a link), followed by a plain caption span. The alt is the upload's file name with its extension, the snapshot's AX tree exposes the image with that name (nameFrom alt), and the live page (curl, 2026-10-23) still serves the same alt. I opened the image itself: it is a photograph of visitors standing around the large city model, with projected questions on the walls. The file name does not describe that picture, so it is not a text alternative (F30: file names used as text alternatives); and if the photo were treated as decorative beside its caption, a non-null alt would still fail (F39), because the image is not ignorable by assistive technology. Either way 1.1.1 fails as the finding says.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The header logo is an image of the text 'MUSEU DO IPIRANGA — USP' (crop and screenshot) and is the only content of the link to the home page; its alt 'logo-museu' is the stem of its file name logo-museu.png, still the same on the live page. The AX tree gives the link the name 'logo-museu' (nameFrom contents); the other 'Museu do Ipiranga' home link in the masthead is hidden (bhf-hidden), so nothing else names it. 'logo-museu' leaves out the museum's name and USP, the text the image shows, and does not say where the link goes, so it is a file-name placeholder rather than an equivalent (F30). 1.1.1 fails as reported; the same name also weakens the link's purpose under 2.4.4.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the footer newsletter sign-up's name field (type=text, name="name", placeholder 'Digite seu Nome', required). It collects the user's own name, a purpose in the WCAG input-purpose list, and HTML supports autocomplete, but the rendered input has no autocomplete attribute. The live page builds the field with the iSend forms script, whose text-field builder sets only type, id, name, placeholder, maxlength, class and required, so this is still true. The name attribute is not a programmatic purpose (H98 needs autocomplete), and the snapshot records Chromium's FormInputAssignedAutocompleteValueToIdOrNameAttributeError for this input, which backs the message. 1.3.5 fails (autocomplete="name", or given-name, would be needed).

judgments.rationale: This is the newsletter sign-up's e-mail field (type=text, name="email", placeholder 'Digite seu E-mail', required). It collects the user's own e-mail address, a listed input purpose, and the rendered input has no autocomplete attribute (it is not even type=email). The live page still builds it with the iSend forms script, which never sets autocomplete. The snapshot records Chromium's FormInputAssignedAutocompleteValueToIdOrNameAttributeError for it, as the message says. The purpose cannot be programmatically determined, so 1.3.5 fails.
